subject.title: [Feature]: Option to force-prepend an opening <think> tag for local reasoning models

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class default-off synthetic `<think>` opener option, or should missing reasoning delimiter handling remain provider-owned through params, model catalog metadata, and provider plugins?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but AGENTS.md and VISION.md make new config/default surfaces and output-format contracts product-sensitive unless existing provider/plugin seams are insufficient.

options.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
options.body: Use existing provider params, thinking profiles, and catalog compatibility metadata unless maintainers confirm they cannot cover the observed local models.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core option
options.body: Add a documented default-off config path, wire it through runner/subscriber params, and prove streaming plus final-message behavior with native-tag and no-tag cases.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject frontend-side delimiter synthesis and ask users to rely on provider/model request settings or prompts instead.

recommendation.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
recommendation.body: Use existing provider params, thinking profiles, and catalog compatibility metadata unless maintainers confirm they cannot cover the observed local models.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current ownership signal is Peter Steinberger's issue review plus current blame across the config and embedded-agent surfaces.
